📌 Deepfake Giveaways: Why No One Will Ever Double Your Crypto

Main Points
⏺ Scammers now use AI deepfakes of famous people on fake livestreams
⏺ The pitch is always the same: send crypto, get double back
⏺ This post explains how the trick works and the one rule that beats it



1️⃣ Core Idea — A "giveaway" that asks you to send money first is not a giveaway. It is a one-way transfer to a stranger's wallet.
2️⃣ Why It Happens — AI can now copy a famous face and voice convincingly. A hijacked channel with a real-looking stream makes it feel official.
3️⃣ Example — This week a fake Tesla stream with a deepfake Elon Musk drew over 500,000 viewers. Coinbase says its AI blocked about $4.7 million that customers tried to send.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — YouTube and X livestreams, QR codes on screen, "limited time" countdowns and fake comment sections full of "I got paid!"
5️⃣ Practical Rule — If anyone promises to send back more crypto than you send, it is a scam. Every time. Close the stream and report it.
Final Thoughts

A crypto transfer can't be undone. No celebrity, exchange or project needs your coins to "verify" a giveaway — real airdrops never ask you to pay first.

Six Hours to Lose the Chair

Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc spent six hours filibustering the vote for Knesset speaker. It bought six hours. By Tuesday night, Likud’s Amir Ohana was out, and Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party had the chair.

Kahana received 66 votes. Likud’s candidate, Ofir Katz, received 52 in a separate ballot. The six parties backing Kahana hold 67 seats, but Ra’am lawmaker Yasser Hujirat was absent. Eisenkot’s four-party bloc supplied 48 votes. Ra’am and the Joint List supplied the other 18. 

The Arab-led parties gave Kahana the votes he needed to win. They have not publicly committed to putting Eisenkot in the prime minister’s office.

United Torah Judaism backed Katz after Kahana’s ballot had already settled the outcome. The timing let the ultra-Orthodox party record its loyalty to Netanyahu without closing the negotiating channel with Eisenkot.

Kahana called for broad agreement on changes to Israel’s checks and balances and pledged that the Knesset under his leadership would comply with court rulings.

The call for agreement requires cooperation from people who just spent six hours trying to delay his election. 

The pledge tells them how he intends to use the chair they couldn’t keep.

📣 MEXC shuts down Visa-linked crypto card less than three months after launch 

🌐 Cryptocurrency exchange MEXC has announced that it will discontinue its Global Card payment services on Nov. 18 at 15:30 UTC, less than two weeks after U.S. authorities issued an order restricting its access to the American financial system. The exchange did not identify the issuing partner or specify whether its decision was directly related to the recent enforcement action by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).

📊 During the maintenance period, customers could transfer their remaining card balances to their exchange accounts, while transactions initiated before the suspension remained subject to normal settlement procedures. MEXC had initially described the interruption as temporary but has now confirmed that the service will not resume as scheduled.

🔗 Cardholders could receive cashback ranging from 4% to 10%, with monthly rewards capped at up to 800 USDT depending on their eligibility. Applications were already unavailable to U.S. residents under the exchange’s regional restrictions. Customers using the card for recurring payments have been advised to cancel their subscriptions or register alternative payment methods to avoid interruptions once the card becomes inactive.
